site_001:n1.prompt:
You are helping me generate our company website using {{vendor}}, a vibe-coding agent. Before starting, ask me for anything you need that's missing: (1) a clear description of the company/product, target audience, and the tone/style we want; (2) key pages or sections required (e.g., home, features, pricing, about, contact); (3) any existing brand assets, logo, color palette, or copy to reuse; (4) an optional Figma file link or existing design to import, or an optional template/community project to start from instead of a blank prompt; (5) our intended domain name, if decided.

Once you have these, use {{vendor}}'s chat-creation capability (the v0.chats.create SDK call) to kick off generation, submitting a single well-structured prompt that includes the company description, desired pages, tone, and any design/template references I provided. This is an asynchronous operation — after creating the chat, poll or check status until the generation completes, and verify the result actually returns a working full-stack site (frontend UI plus any backend logic implied by the prompt) rather than an error or partial output.

If the initial result is close but not right, send follow-up refinement prompts through the same chat to adjust specific elements without breaking what already works, rather than starting over from scratch.

Do not publish or make the site live — this step only produces the generated site for later human review. When generation is verified complete, report back: the chat/session identifier, a summary of what was generated (pages, key features, any backend logic), a preview link if one was returned, and any follow-up prompts you sent and their outcomes.

site_001:n3.prompt:
You are helping me review our newly generated company website before it goes live. The site was built by a vibe-coding agent and needs a thorough pre-launch check, followed by my final human sign-off.

Please ask me for: (1) the staging URL or local path where the site is currently accessible, (2) our company name, tagline, and any brand voice guidelines I have (tone, key messaging, target audience), and (3) a list of pages that should exist (e.g., Home, About, Pricing, Contact).

Once I provide these, please:
1. Crawl every page of the site and check for broken internal and external links, missing images, or 404s.
2. Run a spelling and grammar check across all visible text.
3. Verify all expected pages exist and are reachable from navigation.
4. Check that contact forms, buttons, and calls-to-action link to the correct destinations (even if you can't submit forms).
5. Confirm basic responsiveness/formatting issues aren't obviously broken (e.g., overlapping text, unstyled sections) if you can render or screenshot the pages.
6. Compile a checklist report listing: broken links found, spelling/grammar issues found, missing pages (if any), and any formatting anomalies — each with the specific page/URL and description.
7. Separately, prepare a short summary comparing the site's content and tone against the brand voice guidelines I gave you, flagging anything that seems inconsistent or off-brand, so I can make the final judgment call.

Do not publish, deploy, or make the site live yourself, and do not edit brand copy or design choices on your own judgment — those are subjective calls only I can make. Once your checklist and brand-fit summary are ready, present them to me clearly and stop for human sign-off. I will review your findings, decide what needs fixing, and give explicit approval before publishing.

site_001:n2.prompt:
You are helping me publish our reviewed company website to a global edge CDN with SSL, using an edge-platform vendor I will specify as {{vendor}}. Before starting, ask me for: (1) the {{vendor}} name and confirmation my configured credentials/CLI access are set up, (2) the git repo or build output path for the site, and (3) the custom domain I want attached (e.g. our production domain).

Once you have these, do the following:
1. Connect or confirm the repo/build is linked to {{vendor}} so future git pushes auto-deploy.
2. Trigger a deploy of the current build to {{vendor}}'s edge network using its CLI or dashboard deploy command with your configured credentials.
3. Attach the custom domain to the deployed service via {{vendor}}'s domain-attachment feature.
4. Confirm {{vendor}} is provisioning a free, auto-renewing TLS certificate for the domain (including any wildcard subdomains we use).
5. This deploy is asynchronous — after triggering it, poll {{vendor}}'s deploy/build status until it reports success or failure; do not assume it's live immediately.
6. Once status is 'live', verify: the site loads over HTTPS at the custom domain, the SSL certificate is valid and matches the domain, and static assets are served via edge caching (check response headers or vendor dashboard for CDN confirmation).

Done looks like: the site is reachable at our custom domain over HTTPS with a valid certificate, deploy status shows success, and auto-deploy-on-push is enabled for future updates.

Report back: the live URL, certificate expiry/renewal status, deploy status/log summary, and confirmation that auto-deploy-on-push is active. Flag any failures, pending DNS propagation, or certificate issues you encounter during polling.
